_note: Teaching-accuracy check: 20 concept questions, each sent to the colleague who owns the topic, who must answer with one letter. Code marks it against this key. Draft for Micah to approve.

questions.q: A bond portfolio has a duration of 6 years. If interest rates rise by 1 percentage point, its value will roughly:

options.B: fall about 6%

questions.q: Our liabilities are more rate-sensitive (longer duration) than our assets. Which move hurts surplus?

options.B: Rates fall
options.D: Only a rise in credit spreads

questions.q: Market rates climb well above the rate credited on our annuities. What typically happens?

options.B: Surrenders rise as policyholders chase higher rates

questions.q: Stock markets fall 20%. What happens to the value of the guarantees we wrote on variable annuities?

options.A: It falls, because accounts are smaller
options.B: It rises: we are more likely to have to pay

questions.q: We take on a pension risk transfer deal. What does it add to our balance sheet?

options.B: Long-duration liabilities, plus premium to invest
options.D: Only fee income with no liabilities

questions.q: What is the main job of a surrender charge or market value adjustment?

options.B: To protect the insurer from part of the loss when policyholders leave after rates rise

questions.q: Corporate credit spreads widen but no company defaults. What happens to the prices of the corporate bonds we own?

options.B: They fall
options.C: They stay the same because nobody defaulted

questions.q: What is the key difference between a credit-spread loss and a default loss?

options.B: A spread loss can reverse if spreads tighten; a default is a permanent loss
options.C: A default can reverse; a spread loss is permanent
options.D: Spread losses only affect government bonds

questions.q: Which bonds are below investment grade?

options.B: A

questions.q: Surrenders spike in a frozen market and we have little cash. What is the main risk?

options.B: We must sell assets quickly at a discount (forced selling)

questions.q: Our liquidity ratio falls below 100%. What does that mean in this game?

options.B: Cash and easily sold government bonds would not cover the cash we might need in a 90-day stress

questions.q: Why does this game leave alternatives (including stocks) unhedged?

options.B: Hedging them would give up the extra expected return that helps fund future claims

questions.q: We receive fixed on an interest rate swap. When do we gain?

options.B: When rates fall

questions.q: We hold collateralized swaps that lose value when rates rise. Rates jump. What happens?

options.B: We must post cash collateral now (a margin call)

questions.q: What is the trade-off of buying put options to protect the stock-market guarantees?

options.B: They pay out in a market fall but cost a premium every quarter even if markets rise
options.C: They make us lose more in a fall
options.D: They only protect against rate moves

questions.q: We hold foreign bonds and the US dollar strengthens. Without a currency hedge, what happens to those bonds' value in dollars?

options.B: It falls
options.D: It depends only on interest rates

questions.q: Our largest dealer fails. When does that cost us least?

options.A: When we used one dealer and no collateral
options.B: When we had daily collateral and spread trades across several dealers
options.C: When we had no hedges with gains owed to us and no collateral

questions.q: Why do most insurers not hedge 100% of every risk?

options.B: Full hedging costs the most and gives up gains; a large share is usually enough

questions.q: What is surplus?

options.B: What the company owns minus what it owes

questions.q: What is the core idea of asset liability management?

options.B: Choose investments that behave like the promises to policyholders, so market moves change both sides similarly
options.D: Sell as many policies as possible
